recall_prompt: Say how you would resolve (3x − 18)/(x³(x + 3)) into partial fractions — name each move in order.
insider_note: x³ is the factor x three times, so the form has four fractions and four constants; the roots 0 and −3 give only C and D, and A and B must come from comparing coefficients.

steps.label: Set up the form
steps.margin_note: First mark. x³ is the factor x repeated three times, so it gives THREE fractions: A/x, B/x², C/x³. Then D/(x + 3). Four constants in all.

recall.must_convey: That the repeated factor x³ gives A/x + B/x² + C/x³ and the factor (x + 3) gives D/(x + 3): four constants.
accept: x cubed is repeated three times so write A over x plus B over x squared plus C over x cubed plus D over x plus three
four fractions, three for the powers of x and one for x plus three
A by x plus B by x square plus C by x cube plus D by x plus 3
x cube ante x moodu sarlu repeat, kabatti A by x, B by x square, C by x cube, plus D by x plus three
write one fraction for each power of x up to three and one for x plus three

steps.why: A factor repeated n times needs n fractions, one for each power from 1 up to n. x³ therefore needs three, and forgetting any one of them makes the identity impossible to satisfy.
common_mistakes: Writing only C/x³ + D/(x + 3) and missing A/x and B/x².
Writing (Ax² + Bx + C)/x³ as one fraction; it equals the three fractions but is not the marked form.

steps.label: Clear the denominators
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply by x³(x + 3). A keeps x²(x + 3), B keeps x(x + 3), C keeps (x + 3), D keeps x³. The power of x left with each constant goes down by one each time.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying through gives 3x − 18 = Ax²(x + 3) + Bx(x + 3) + C(x + 3) + Dx³.
accept: multiply both sides by x cubed into x plus three to get three x minus eighteen equals A x squared into x plus three plus B x into x plus three plus C into x plus three plus D x cubed
clear the denominators and A keeps x squared, B keeps x, C keeps nothing and D keeps x cubed
multiply through by the whole denominator to get an identity in x
x cube into x plus three tho multiply cheste A x square into x plus three plus B x into x plus three plus C into x plus three plus D x cube vastundi
remove the fractions by multiplying with x cubed times x plus three

steps.why: Each fraction over a power of x keeps the difference between x³ and its own power: x² for A, x for B, none for C. That pattern is what lets x = 0 isolate C and the coefficients isolate A and B.
common_mistakes: Giving the C term x(x + 3) or x²(x + 3) instead of (x + 3).
Giving the D term (x + 3) instead of x³.

steps.label: Find the constants
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Two roots, 0 and −3, give C and D. Then compare x³ for A and x² for B. Expand only the coefficients you need; no need to expand everything.

recall.must_convey: That x = −3 gives D = 1, x = 0 gives C = −6, comparing x³ gives A + D = 0 so A = −1, and comparing x² gives 3A + B = 0 so B = 3.
accept: put x equals minus three to get D equals one, x equals zero to get C equals minus six, then compare x cubed to get A equals minus one and x squared to get B equals three
two substitutions give D one and C minus six and the coefficients of x cubed and x squared give A minus one and B three
D is one C is minus six A is minus one and B is three
x equals minus three pedithe D one, x equals zero pedithe C minus six, x cube compare cheste A minus one, x square compare cheste B three
the last two constants come from equating the x cubed and x squared coefficients

steps.why: With only two roots and four constants, two constants must come from coefficients. x³ appears in Ax²(x + 3) and Dx³, giving A + D; x² appears in 3Ax² from the A term and Bx² from the B term, giving 3A + B. The left side has no x³ or x², so both equal 0.
common_mistakes: Writing 3(−3) − 18 as −9 + 18 = 9 instead of −27, which makes D come out as −1.
Reading the x² coefficient as B alone and forgetting the 3A from Ax²(x + 3).
Stopping after C and D and never finding A and B.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Four fractions with their signs: −1/x + 3/x² − 6/x³ + 1/(x + 3). Write the original fraction on the left.

accept: the answer is minus one over x plus three over x squared minus six over x cubed plus one over x plus three
minus one by x plus three by x square minus six by x cube plus one by x plus three
write minus 1 by x plus 3 by x squared minus 6 by x cubed plus 1 by x plus 3 as the answer
final answer minus one by x plus three by x square minus six by x cube plus one by x plus three ani rasali
put A B C D back into the four fractions with their signs

steps.why: The resolved form with all four fractions and correct signs is what the examiner marks. A and C are negative, so two of the four terms are subtracted.
common_mistakes: Writing +1/x after finding A = −1, or +6/x³ after finding C = −6.
Dropping one of the four fractions in the final line.
Not checking: put x = 1 in the identity, −15 = −4 + 12 − 24 + 1. If the two sides differ, a constant is wrong.
